title: Agaseke basket weaving
summary: The agaseke is Rwanda's lidded basket: taller than it is wide, with a flat round base and a sloping, cone-shaped cover. Sisal and grass are coiled in rising rings and bound with strands dyed purple, green, black, yellow or red, and triangles and zigzags are set into the wall.
howToPlay: The lit case above the bench shows the agaseke as it should finish. Look at how its pattern climbs the curve.
Choose a strand colour below the basket, then lay each stitch across the front of the ring. The gold ring marks the next place and the strip under the basket shows the row in hand.
Work up from the base, one ring at a time, so each ring lines up with the steps in the case.
Press Check when every stitch is laid. Undo takes the last stitch back.
rules: The basket body is built from 9 rings of 13 stitches, laid from the base upward, one ring at a time. The lid is already woven.
Each stitch takes one of three strand colours: pale sisal, black or madder brown.
The score is the share of stitches whose colour matches the pattern, counted beyond what laying only the commonest colour would earn. Three stars need 88, two need 65 and one needs 40.
Undo takes back the last stitch. A basket left plain earns no stars.
heritageNote: Agaseke baskets are made mostly by women across Rwanda and are traditionally given to carry food and gifts to a family visit or a wedding, so the lidded shape has come to stand for goodwill between families. Cooperatives keep the named patterns and the tight coil alive today.
